title: 3XFlag-pATn5 Protein Purification and MEDS-loading (5x scale, 2L volume)
author: Terri Bryson
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8yrhxv6
materials: Make buffers and media. See Materials section .

Need 400 mL, HEGX+PI today; make a total of 1L HEGX and add PI tablets as needed each day. Remove pellets from freezer, thaw on ice and resuspend together in a combined total of 200 mL of chilled HEGX Buffer with Roche Complete EDTA free protease inhibitor (PI) tablets. Keep on ice while working.

Chitin Binding: The remainder of the protocol is carried out at 4 °C or on ice. All buffers should be chilled on ice prior to use. In 4 °C, room prepare 10x Econo-Pac® Chromatography Columns (BIO-RAD 732-1010), each holds 20 mL Set-up columns (we use a rack intended for Qiagen Maxi-preps, figure B). Gently invert Chitin Resin (NEB S6651S) to fully suspend and add 2.5mL to each column. Wash each with 20 mL of HEGX Buffer, drain immediately, don’t collect anything. Do not let resin dry out prior to addition of sample.

In vitro activity assay is performed on 150 ng HMW Lambda DNA (NEB# N3011). Unloaded pATn5 or loaded pATN5 without MgCl 2 should have no impact on HMW DNA, loaded pATN5 in digestion buffer should digest HMW DNA to a smear. See figure F.

steps.title: Streak glycerol stock on LB-Amp plate
steps.instruction: Streak the E. coli glycerol stock containing the pTXB1‑rbs_3XFlag‑pATn5‑FL plasmid onto an LB‑Amp 100 µg/mL agar plate and incubate overnight at 37 °C.

steps.title: Patch single colony for later use
steps.instruction: Select a single colony, make a patch plate for later use, and keep the patch plate for use within one week.

steps.title: Inoculate starter culture
steps.instruction: Using a sterile toothpick, swipe the bacterial patch and inoculate 30 mL of LB broth containing carbenicillin 100 µg/mL; shake for approximately 4 h.

steps.title: Pre‑warm large LB‑carbenicillin volume
steps.instruction: Add 1970 mL of LB with carbenicillin 100 µg/mL to a 6 L flask and place it at 37 °C so the medium is warm at the time of dilution.

steps.title: Scale up culture and monitor OD600
steps.instruction: Inoculate the 1970 mL culture with the entire 30 mL starter culture, shake at 37 °C and monitor OD600 periodically until it reaches 0.5–0.7 (approximately 3 h).

steps.title: Cool culture before induction
steps.instruction: Transfer the culture to a cold room and let it cool for about 1 h.

steps.title: Induce expression with IPTG
steps.instruction: Add fresh 1 M IPTG to the cooled culture to a final concentration of 0.25 mM and incubate on an 18 °C shaker overnight.

steps.title: Harvest cells by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Divide the induced culture into six 500 mL bottles and centrifuge at 9500 rcf, 4 °C for 1 h in a GS‑3 rotor (Sorvall RC5C).

steps.title: Freeze pellets and store
steps.instruction: Freeze the bacterial pellets in a dry‑ice/ethanol bath and store at –80 °C until further processing.

steps.title: Resuspend pellets and aliquot on ice
steps.instruction: Combine the pellets, resuspend in lysis buffer, and divide the suspension into four clean 100 mL plastic beakers that are nested inside a larger beaker filled with ice (see figure A).

steps.title: Sonicate lysates with cooling intervals
steps.instruction: While keeping the samples on ice, sonicate each beaker 10–12 times for 45 s per pulse at 50 % duty cycle, output level 7 on a Branson Sonifier 250 with the micro‑tip; between pulses keep the beaker on ice, stir gently with a 2 mL serological pipette, and allow at least 45 s rest between pulses. Keep the tip centered to avoid foaming; if foam forms, let it settle or remove with a pipette.

steps.title: Clarify lysate by high‑speed spin
steps.instruction: Transfer each sonicated lysate to a fresh 50 mL conical tube and centrifuge for 30 min at 4 °C, 16000 × g.

steps.title: Prepare chitin column with yellow cap
steps.instruction: Add a yellow cap to the bottom of each chitin affinity column.

steps.title: Load lysate onto chitin resin
steps.instruction: Slowly add the cleared lysate supernatant to the chitin resin to prevent bubble formation.

steps.title: Incubate column overnight at 4 °C
steps.instruction: Cap the column tightly and place it on a nutator at 4 °C overnight. Check for leakage after 15 min and 30 min; if leakage occurs, wrap both ends with parafilm.

steps.title: Drain unbound fraction and collect washes
steps.instruction: Remove the yellow cap, hang the column over a collection tube, and uncap to drain the unbound fraction into 50 mL tubes (keep on ice or at 4 °C).

steps.title: Wash column twice with HEGX buffer
steps.instruction: Wash the column two times with 20 mL HEGX buffer each; collect the first wash in 50 mL tubes (keep cold) and discard the second wash.

steps.title: Prepare HEGX+PI buffer with DTT
steps.instruction: Make 65 mL of HEGX buffer containing 100 mM DTT (HEGX + PI) and add 6 mL of this buffer to each column.

steps.title: Incubate column with HEGX+PI overnight
steps.instruction: Cap the column tightly and nutate in the cold room for approximately 48 h.

steps.title: Drain resin and record elution volume
steps.instruction: Remove the column from the rack, drain the unbound fraction into 15 mL conical tubes, combine the fractions, cover the resin with an additional 2 mL buffer, and store at 4 °C until purification is verified. Record the elution volume (≈ 50 mL).

steps.title: Concentrate protein using centrifugal filter
steps.instruction: Spin the eluted protein in an Eppendorf 5804R at 2880 × g, 4 °C for 1 h, checking every 20 min; do not let the volume fall below the top of the filter.

steps.title: Recover concentrate and rinse filter
steps.instruction: Collect the concentrate from the upper filter (~7 mL) and add 0.5 mL of buffer from the lower catch tube to rinse the filter; total recovered volume ≈ 9 mL.

steps.title: Add glycerol to protein concentrate
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of sterile 80 % glycerol to the concentrated protein (final glycerol concentration ≈ 50 % when combined with glycerol from dialysis).

steps.title: Store concentrated protein at –20 °C
steps.instruction: Aliquot and store the glycerol‑containing protein at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare BSA standards for gel
steps.instruction: Dilute the 250 ng/µL BSA stock to 125 ng/µL and load increasing volumes onto the gel as standards.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE gel
steps.instruction: Load all samples onto the gel and run at 30 mA for ~1 h or until the loading dye front reaches the bottom of the gel.

steps.title: Stain gel with Coomassie
steps.instruction: Transfer the gel to a covered dish containing Coomassie stain, gently shake for at least 1 h up to overnight at room temperature.

steps.title: Destain gel and absorb excess dye
steps.instruction: Replace the stain with destain solution and place a rolled paper towel in the dish to absorb excess Coomassie dye.

steps.title: Assemble Slide‑A‑Lyzer dialysis cassettes
steps.instruction: Assemble two Slide‑A‑Lyzer 10K MWCO cassettes: attach a 1 ¼‑inch binder clip to hold a 2‑inch stir bar, remove the clip handles, secure a foam float with an 18‑inch zip tie, hydrate the cassette per the manufacturer’s instructions, and anchor the cassette in a dialysis beaker by clipping the zip‑tie tail to the beaker lip.

steps.title: Load cassettes with protein sample
steps.instruction: Using an 18‑gauge needle, load each cassette with 25 mL of the protein sample following the product literature.

steps.title: First dialysis in Tn5 buffer (1–2 h)
steps.instruction: Place both cassettes in a 4 L beaker containing 2.5 L of Tn5 dialysis buffer; add DTT to a final concentration of 1.7 mM just before use, and dialyze for 1–2 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Overnight dialysis in fresh Tn5 buffer
steps.instruction: Transfer the cassettes to fresh 2.5 L Tn5 dialysis buffer (again add DTT to 1.7 mM just before use) and dialyze overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Recover dialyzed protein and store on ice
steps.instruction: Recover the sample from each cassette, combine into a fresh 50 mL conical tube, keep on ice or at 4 °C; recovered volume ≈ 42 mL. The sample may be stored overnight if needed.

steps.title: Resuspend oligos in annealing buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend single‑stranded, salt‑free oligos (Eurofins) to 200 µM in Annealing Buffer (10 mM Tris, pH 8, 50 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA).

steps.title: Mix complementary oligos and aliquot
steps.instruction: Mix equal volumes of complementary oligos at equimolar concentration in a 1.5 mL microfuge tube: 400 µL Tn5ME‑rev + 400 µL Tn5ME‑A → 800 µL, split into 4 tubes of 200 µL each; repeat with Tn5ME‑rev + Tn5ME‑B for another 4 tubes.

steps.title: Anneal oligos using ANNEALOL program
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in an MJ Cycler PTC‑200 and run the ANNEALOL program: 95 °C for 2 min, then decrease temperature in 5 °C steps, holding each step for 5 min, ending with 25 °C for 5 min, then hold at 8 °C. Store annealed oligos at –20 °C.

steps.title: Verify annealing on acrylamide gel
steps.instruction: Run both single‑stranded and double‑stranded oligos on a 6 % acrylamide 1× TBE gel with the following lanes: 1) 1 kb+ marker 3 µL, 2) Rev + ME‑A 1 µL + 1 µL 6× Fermentas Orange Loading Dye + 6 µL TE, 3) Rev + ME‑B same as 2, 4) Rev alone, 5) ME‑A alone (0.5 µL), 6) ME‑B alone (0.5 µL), 7) 100 bp marker 3 µL.

steps.title: Assemble Tn5ME‑oligo complexes
steps.instruction: Combine 600 µL of 100 µM Tn5ME‑rev/A oligo, 600 µL of 100 µM Tn5ME‑rev/B oligo, and 7.5 mL of 3×Flag‑pATn5 (in 50 % glycerol); incubate ~50 min at room temperature and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare MEDS reaction mix per sample
steps.instruction: For each sample combine: 150 ng high‑molecular‑weight DNA, 4 µL 5× TAPS‑MgCl₂‑PEG8000 (use water for no‑digestion‑buffer controls), 5 µL pATn5‑MEDS complex, and add nuclease‑free H₂O to a final volume of 20 µL.

steps.title: Incubate reaction at 55 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the reaction mix for 7 min at 55 °C.

steps.title: Add SDS to inactivate Tn5
steps.instruction: Add 2 µL of 1 % SDS to each reaction to release and inactivate Tn5.

steps.title: Incubate after SDS addition
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture for 7 min at room temperature or at 55 °C.

steps.title: Add proteinase K to degrade pATn5
steps.instruction: Add 0.63 µL proteinase K (20 mg/mL) to each reaction.

steps.title: Incubate after proteinase K addition
steps.instruction: Incubate for 7 min at 55 °C.

steps.title: Analyze products on agarose gel
steps.instruction: Run the final samples on a 0.7 % agarose gel in 1× TAE with the following lanes: 1) 150 ng HMW lambda DNA, 2) 1 kb+ MW marker, 3) pATn5 (‑) MEDS, 4) pATn5 (+) MEDS, (‑) digestion buffer, 5) pATn5 (+) MEDS, (+) digestion buffer, 6) pATn5 [batch 2] (+) MEDS, (+) digestion buffer.

description: Replace destain with water, scan gel for notes.
